title: Is it Possible to Get New Teeth in a Day? Explore the All-on-4 Dental Implant Procedure
excerpt: New teeth in a day? Is it possible? This article explores the all-on-4 teeth in a day dental implant procedure, highlighting the benefits and risk factors.
body:
Are you tired of dealing with missing teeth or uncomfortable dentures? For suitable patients, a full arch of fixed temporary teeth can be fitted on the same day as implant surgery, a treatment often called “teeth in a day”. This article explains how it works, who it may suit and the factors that affect the result.

What Are Teeth in a Day?

Teeth in a day, also referred colloquially to as “teeth in a hour” or “same day teeth” or as “same-day dental implants” or “immediate dental implants”, is a treatment in which a fixed temporary bridge is attached to the implants on the day of surgery. The final bridge is made and fitted once the implants have integrated with the bone, generally three to six months later.

Exploring the All-on-4 Dental Implant Process

What Is a Dental Implant?

A dental implant is a titanium post that is surgically placed in the jaw bone to serve as a replacement for a missing tooth root. This post provides a stable foundation for a crown, bridge, or denture, restoring both the function and appearance of natural teeth.

How Are Teeth in a Day Different?

The traditional dental implant process involves multiple visits to the dentist over several months. With teeth in a day, the implants and a fixed temporary bridge are placed in one surgical appointment, so suitable patients do not go without teeth while the implants heal. Follow-up visits are still needed, and the final bridge is fitted later.

What Can I Expect During Surgery?

During the teeth in a day procedure, any diseased teeth are removed, and dental implants are placed directly into the jawbone. Generally, four implants made from titanium are used for each arch in a minimally invasive procedure allowing the surgeon to work with the available bone in your jaw, without the need of bone grafting, in a technique called “all-on-4 dental implants“.

These implants act as a foundation which allows the placement of a fixed set of teeth. Thanks to an in-house 3D intraoral scanner, printer and software technology, a complete digital impression of the patient’s mouth is taken to fully map the teeth and gums. With this data then, a custom made temporary denture, also called temporary bridge, is 3-D printed, painted in the gum area, cured in a light cure box for about one minute and it is ready for the patient immediately.

Possible Benefits of Teeth in a Day

1. Fixed Temporary Teeth From the Day of Surgery

For suitable patients, a fixed temporary bridge is attached on the day of surgery, so there is no period without teeth while waiting for the final bridge. A soft diet is needed while the implants heal.

2. Fewer Surgical Procedures

Because extractions and implant placement are often done in the same operation, and bone grafting can sometimes be avoided, some patients need fewer surgical procedures. Recovery varies from person to person, and your surgeon will explain what to expect in your case.

3. Function and Appearance

Missing teeth can affect eating, speaking and how people feel about their smile. A fixed bridge may help with these, although individual results vary.

Is Teeth-in-a-Day Implant Treatment Right for You?

Here is a short – non exhaustive – list of indications for this surgical procedure.

Are You Missing Teeth?

Teeth in a day may be an option for people who are missing most or all of their teeth in one or both jaws, or whose remaining teeth cannot be saved. A consultation and 3D scan show whether it suits you.

Do You have Adequate Bone Density?

If you have been missing teeth for a long time, your bone density might have regressed over time in the mandible (lower jaw) or maxilla (upper jaw). Your surgeon will be able to verify this through 3D dental x-rays and other software technology. Depending on the available bone density in the upper jaw, the surgeon might recommend the placement zygomatic implants, an advanced technique particularly useful in those with severe bone loss in their upper jaw.

Do You Want Immediate Results?

If you want to avoid the long waiting periods associated with traditional dental implant procedures, teeth in a day may be worth discussing with your surgeon.

Are You Looking for a Convenient Option?

Teeth in a day can mean fewer surgical appointments, although reviews and the final bridge still need several visits.

What Factors Play a Role in the Success of Same-day Dental Implants?

The dental and medical history of the patient is critical for the success of the surgery. Here is a – non exhaustive – list of factors that add risk to the success of the procedure.

  • Heavy smoking: Smokers must note they are two and a half times more likely to experience failure than non-smokers. The relative risk of implant failure is significantly higher in patients who smoke 20 cigarettes or more per day compared to nonsmokers. Furthermore, heavy smokers have significantly higher chances of post-surgery infection rates.
  • Gum disease: Those who suffer from gum disease will need to have the condition successfully treated prior to proceeding with implants. A good gum health is pivotal for the success rate of any dental placement procedure.
  • Diabetes: Patients with diabetes usually have co-morbidities (existing medical conditions) and have, therefore, a higher risk of post-op infection as this condition slows down the body’s ability to fight infections.
  • Oral hygiene: It is important the patient understands the importance of good oral hygiene and is able to undertake daily brushing and flossing using correct techniques prior to the placement of implants.

Conclusion

Teeth in a day is one way to replace a full arch of teeth with fixed implant-supported teeth, with a temporary bridge fitted on the day of surgery for suitable patients. Whether it suits you depends on your bone, your general health and your goals. Talk to your dentist, or arrange a consultation with an oral and maxillofacial surgeon, to find out whether it is right for you.

title: Why Wisdom Teeth Removal Before Age 25 May Be Easier than Later
excerpt: Wisdom teeth removal before the age of 25 is recommended in certain cases before it may cause any significant problems.
body:
Removal of a troublesome wisdom tooth is a very common procedure in dentistry, and when a wisdom tooth does need to come out, removal is often simpler in younger adults. In this article, we explain what to look out for and why the timing can matter. Surgery in older adults can take longer and may carry a higher risk of complications.

What are Wisdom Teeth?

Wisdom teeth is the common name for the third set of molars. These teeth do not erupt through the gums usually until people are in their late teens or early 20s. There are four wisdom teeth in total but not every person has all of them fully formed.

What are Impacted Wisdom Teeth?

Sometimes there is not enough space at the back of the jaw for a wisdom tooth to come through, so this can become “impacted” which means the tooth is partially or fully trapped in your gums in different positions and angles. Some impacted third molars will never cause any issues, they just stay buried in their position. However, other impacted wisdom teeth may cause serious issues, including infection in the surrounding gum tissue.

Here are Some Issues Troublesome Wisdom Teeth Can Create

Impacted wisdom teeth can cause the following issues:

  • Pain: in the neighbouring teeth caused by the pressure of the wisdom tooth, or caused by an infection.
  • Infection: particularly at the top of the tooth when this is about to erupt.
  • Cyst: this is a sac of fluid that can form around the wisdom tooth (often unerupted) and may displace it. It may destroy the bone and damage other surrounding teeth and gums.
  • Ulcer: this can happen when a wisdom tooth in the upper jawbone pushes sideways out of the gum and rubs against the inside of the cheek.
  • Resorption Cavity: this happens when an impacted tooth pushes towards and hits the molar next to it causing damage to both teeth. This is not very common.
  • A food trap: when food becomes trapped between a wisdom tooth and its adjacent molar increasing the risk of tooth decay.

When Should Wisdom Teeth Be Removed?

Not every wisdom tooth needs to be removed. When a wisdom tooth is causing problems, or is likely to, removal between the ages of 17 and 25 is often simpler, because the roots may not be fully formed and the surrounding bone is softer. Your surgeon will advise whether and when removal is recommended for you.

Indications for Early Wisdom Teeth Extraction

The surgical extraction of wisdom teeth is indicated (recommended) for the following reasons:

  1. The concerned tooth or gum area has started to cause pain
  2. There is not enough room in the mouth for the tooth to push through
  3. Orthodontic work (braces) may be needed as space is needed
  4. When the other molars around the impacted tooth need to be protected
  5. Last, but one of the most important reasons is when the impacted wisdom tooth in the lower jaw is close to major nerves like the inferior alveolar nerve or the lingual nerve which may complicate the extraction process.

Your dentist or oral surgeon may need to take x-rays to determine the need to remove wisdom teeth.

If you have been advised that a wisdom tooth may need to come out, wisdom teeth removal is usually easier to plan before problems develop.

The Wisdom Teeth Removal Procedure

Usually, a general dentist will refer patients to an oral surgeon for wisdom teeth extraction procedures. The surgeon will use local anaesthetic, general anaesthetic, or sedation therapy to make the patient comfortable depending on the individual clinical case. During the procedure the surgeon will then make an incision (cut) to open the gums and a small portion of the bone to be able to extract the impacted tooth. The tooth may have to be divided into small sections to be able to be extracted safely. Lastly, the incision is closed with stitches that will dissolve in a few days or may need a follow-up appointment to be removed.
